title: Every allocation Instance carries a flag stating whether its own risk model is fully implemented or still pending
content:
A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.3 defines a status that sits on every Active Instance: "The `RRC Framework Full Implementation Coverage` status defines whether the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model... or a pending risk model... If the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model the status is `Covered`. If... a pending risk model the status is `Pending`." Pattern's Maple USDC instance is marked **`Covered`** (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.1).

This is a second-order disclosure and an unusual one. Most risk frameworks publish a number; this one publishes a claim about the *provenance* of the number. A required-risk-capital figure derived from a provisional model is not the same kind of fact as one derived from a finished model, and the flag forces that distinction to travel alongside the figure instead of being lost in it.

The consequence is that risk capital can be computed for a position before the modelling work is complete — the framework does not block deployment pending a finished model, it labels it. That is a deliberate trade of precision for operability, and the label is what keeps the trade honest: an aggregate built from many `Pending` instances can be recognized as weakly grounded without re-deriving it.

Because the status lives on the instance rather than on the Agent, it also becomes a comparable, auditable field across the whole ecosystem — one can ask what fraction of deployed capital sits behind finished models.
description: RRC Framework Full Implementation Coverage reads Covered or Pending depending on which model computes the Instance Financial RRC, so model maturity is disclosed per position.
